external_invariants: FP32 everywhere: weights loaded with dtype=torch.float32 and compute kept in FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False.
Deterministic seed policy from common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), 4 CPU threads, 1 inter-op thread.

Model identity and mode unchanged: ResNetForImageClassification initialized from the frozen request assets dir (local_files_only=True, microsoft/resnet-18 weights, num_params=11689512) and kept in eval() on context['device'].

Input construction is frozen: pixels.npy (3 preprocessed FP32 NCHW 224x224 real images) extended to the workload batch via arange(batch) % 3 then .contiguous(), transferred to GPU once outside timing.

Work amount is one full batch forward per measured invocation with no internal iteration, no caching between repeats, and no change to batch (32), architecture, precision, data or output requirements.

Outputs are the full [batch,1000] logits and argmax class ids; quality requires require_exact_top1 (torch.equal on argmax over all 1000 classes) plus torch.testing.assert_close at logits_atol=logits_rtol=1e-4, and the source's negative control must reject a +1 corruption of the reference.

Metric semantics preserved: latency_ms is the wall time of the single synchronized forward; images_per_second = batch*1000/latency_ms is the reciprocal of the same boundary; peak_allocated_bytes is torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() for the measured invocation.

The offline workload row is preserved verbatim, including the memory goal's images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio 0.95 guard, which is scoped to the memory goal and not to the latency objective (which carries no constraints).

selection.rationale: Current accepted version (revision ad45c7ec with bundle trial-9c6f5280d7-param-ad514673 installed, clean objective 3.6742565 ms vs parent 4.210417) is measured GPU-saturated: execution_timeline on this exact revision shows 60 CUDA kernels with active union 3617.53us and only 2.62us of inter-kernel gaps (profiled wall 3.93ms; cProfile self-time is 3.44ms cuda_synchronize wait), so launch/dispatch headroom is exhausted and the CUDA-graph replay routes (captured/cuda_graph_replay) are working. Per-call kernel attribution (call-resources, all 60 kernels owned by module call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa): conv compute 2900.1us + winograd tile generation 79.0us + offsets 12.4us = 2991.6us (82.7%) already runs at ~20 TFLOP/s effective FP32 with winograd under the frozen no-TF32, cudnn.benchmark=False policy - no legal conv headroom is claimed. The remaining measured slack is the memory-bound stem chain: the candidate Triton _bias_relu writes the 32x64x112x112 (205.5MB) stem activation, then max_pool_forward_nchw re-reads those 205.5MB and writes 25.7MB at only ~1.26TB/s achieved - the least efficient kernel in the window - for ~642MB of HBM traffic total, followed by _bias_relu 290.5us/9 and _add_bias_relu 139.4us/8 kernels already near ~2.1TB/s. Per-channel bias and ReLU commute with a spatial 2x2 max, so one fused conv-epilogue kernel (read conv output once, apply bias+ReLU while pooling, write only the 25.7MB pooled tensor) removes ~411MB of round-trip traffic (measured ~180-270us at the observed achieved bandwidths) and is bitwise-identical algebra to the accepted candidate (same element selected, same per-element additions). Everything affected - the fused stem epilogue, the unchanged conv/pool/linear ops, and the lazy capture/warmup/verified-replay path it must be built into per binding-contract - lies inside the one coherent editable boundary already owned by this group: the ResNetForImageClassification forward (module call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa). The other observed groups are not targets: 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb is the frozen measurement boundary (project.invoke), d9e5d004/9251a36a/f60289be/798df708 are discovery record_function enter/exit hooks with 0us CUDA time, and ca15d8d1515e55fb8500 is the replay-path aten::clone of the [32,1000] logits (1.44us DtoD), none of which the stem fusion needs to touch.
selection.hypothesis: Composing on the installed whole-bundle replacement of group eca3643289778aea5af3 and replacing the stem epilogue (separate _bias_relu kernel + aten max_pool2d re-reading the same 205.5MB activation) with one fused bias+ReLU+2x2-maxpool Triton kernel - captured inside the existing side-stream warmup -> CUDA-graph capture -> verified replay flow, with the eager fused path and parent fallback preserved for non-matching signatures - reduces latency_ms from the accepted 3.6742565 by roughly 0.15-0.28ms (~4-7%, hypothesis ~3.39-3.52ms), because it deletes ~411MB of measured HBM round-trips (the max_pool kernel alone is 183.6us and runs at ~1.26TB/s while neighboring pointwise kernels achieve ~2.1TB/s) while conv (2991.6us, ~FP32 roofline), workload, batch, precision, measurement boundaries and quality checks stay untouched. Numerical output is expected to be identical to the accepted candidate (bias/ReLU commute with spatial max; same per-element sums), which already passed at max_abs_error 9.5e-6 with exact top1; measured AB/BA timing, not this estimate, decides acceptance.

proposal.rationale: Compose on the installed whole-bundle replacement of group eca3643289778aea5af3 by explicitly replacing bundle trial-9c6f5280d7-param-ad514673 (accepted at 3.6742565 ms vs parent 4.210417, quality pass at max_abs_error 9.5e-6 with exact top1) and re-owning its entire behavior at module call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa: eval BatchNorm2d folded into bias-free conv weights at build time, fused residual add+bias+ReLU and conv bias+ReLU Triton pointwise kernels, identical aten conv2d/adaptive_avg_pool2d/linear ops under the frozen FP32/no-TF32/cudnn.benchmark=False policy, the lazy side-stream warmup -> CUDA-graph capture -> verified replay flow with input-signature (shape/stride/dtype/device/data_ptr) guards, the eager fused path, and parent fallback for unsupported signatures. previous-feedback.txt contains no failure to repair: the previous trial was accepted, and its nsys/execution_timeline evidence (60 kernels, all in graph id 2, active union 3617.53us, 2.62us gaps) plus call-resources per-kernel attribution is what motivates this increment. The one measured remaining slack is the memory-bound stem epilogue: the candidate _bias_relu kernel writes the 32x64x112x112 stem activation (210.0us, grid 2048x13) and aten max_pool_forward_nchw then re-reads that activation and writes the 32x64x56x56 pooled tensor (183.6us at ~1.26TB/s achieved, the least efficient kernel in the window) - about 642MB of HBM traffic for ~230MB of useful payload. Correction to the selection note: the installed stem pooler in transformers 5.16.1 is nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1) (ResNetEmbeddings.__init__), not a 2x2/stride-2/pad-0 pool; the fused Triton kernel therefore implements exactly that 3x3/stride-2/pad-1 geometry with masked border loads (padded lanes read -inf, the max identity), guarded to accept only this geometry plus dilation 1 and ceil_mode False. Per-channel bias and ReLU commute with a spatial max for finite floats (IEEE addition and ReLU are monotonic, so max_i relu(x_i + b) == relu(max_i x_i + b) bitwise, same element selected, same per-element sums), so one fused kernel now reads the raw conv output once, applies bias+ReLU while pooling, and writes only the 25.7MB pooled tensor, deleting roughly 411MB of measured round trips (~0.15-0.28ms at the observed 1.26-2.1TB/s). CPU validation with the worker python: the kernel's window/index emulation is bitwise equal to relu(x+b) then max_pool2d(3,2,1) for 112x112 and odd/edge sizes, the plan build on the frozen assets selects the fused stem step, and the full eager pipeline matches the parent module forward to 4.1e-6 (FP32 reassociation only, same as the accepted bundle). Conv compute (~2991.6us at ~20 TFLOP/s effective FP32), workload, batch=32, precision, measurement boundaries and quality checks are untouched; measured AB/BA timing, not this estimate, decides acceptance. Route labels (cuda_graph_replay, eager_fused_stem_pool, captured, capture_failed, capture_verification_failed, graph_replay_failed, parent_fallback_unsupported_signature, setup_failure:*) remain diagnostic self-reports; the graph is captured during a real invocation on the live input storage, so replay re-executes the actual accepted work on current inputs each invocation.

setup_work.parameter_transform: At build time (torch.inference_mode(False), torch.no_grad(), so tensors stay usable in any later context; unchanged from the accepted bundle): fold the 20 eval BatchNorm2d affines (gamma/sqrt(var+eps), beta-mean*scale) into contiguous FP32 conv-weight copies (~44.7MB, convs stay bias-free so cudnn heuristics see identical shapes), per-channel biases with the shortcut bias pre-added per basic layer, and clone the detached classifier weight/bias (~2.1MB). Original parameters are untouched, so parent fallback and framework restore keep exact parent semantics. The stem conv keeps its folded weight/bias but its epilogue is now planned as one fused bias+ReLU+3x3/stride-2/pad-1 max-pool step.
setup_work.first_cuda_invocation: Triton JIT compile of the three kernels (_bias_relu, _add_bias_relu, and the new _bias_relu_pool3x3s2p1), side-stream warmup, CUDA graph capture of the fused static sequence, and a replay-vs-eager verification at atol=rtol=1e-4 before the graph is used - all on the first candidate CUDA call inside the adapter's real forward/inference_mode context, which precedes the timed repeats (warmup=2, quality checks first); later timed invocations replay.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates ~46.8MB of folded/cloned FP32 parameters that stay alive for the warm-model lifecycle (same as the accepted bundle; the fused stem kernel adds no new persistent parameters). The CUDA graph retains a private pool roughly the size of the activation high-water mark, which increases reserved/lifecycle_reserved bytes; because transient activations (now including the pooled stem output instead of the full 102.8MB relu'd stem activation plus its 25.7MB pooled copy) move into the graph pool, the per-run peak_allocated_bytes counter is expected to fall - an allocator-scope effect, not a physical-memory saving, and none of these counters measures the graph pool's reserved bytes as allocated.

quality_risks: The fused stem epilogue reassociates bias/ReLU with the spatial max; for finite floats this is bitwise identical to the accepted candidate's separate kernels (IEEE addition and ReLU are monotonic; CPU emulation of the exact kernel index math is bitwise equal to relu(x+b) then max_pool2d(3,2,1) for 112x112 and odd/edge sizes). Residual logits shift versus the eager parent remains the accepted bundle's FP32 reassociation (~1e-6..1e-5, previously measured max_abs_error 9.5e-6), within atol=rtol=1e-4; exact top1 can only flip if two classes are nearly tied in the reference.
Triton maximum drops NaN where aten propagates it; the frozen fixture and weights are finite, so no NaN is expected on this path (same caveat as the accepted bundle's pointwise kernels).

The fusion guard accepts only MaxPool2d(kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False) with contiguous CUDA input; every other geometry, non-contiguous input, or Triton failure takes the accepted bundle's separate relu(x+b) then F.max_pool2d sequence bitwise (self.broken latch, guarded during capture so a capture-time failure disables the graph instead of producing wrong output).

CUDA graph capture/replay can fail on unusual worker states; every graph step stays guarded (capture_failed, capture_verification_failed, graph_replay_failed route labels) and degrades to the general eager fused path, never to wrong output. The graph reads the live input storage, so mutated input contents are recomputed on each replay; different tensor objects with non-matching signatures take the eager path.

Graph replay does not re-execute the parent's inner Python calls; the earlier whole bundle is explicitly replaced and eliminated_calls lists every descendant again, with equivalent conv/pool/linear work continuing inside the replacement. If the evaluator rebuilds the input tensor per invocation (different data_ptr each call), the graph guard routes every call to the eager fused path: still correct, with the BN-fold, fused pointwise and fused stem-pool savings only.

plan.rationale: Frozen objective is one offline batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward on a single GPU; observations.json marks communication not_applicable, so nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and any per-collective byte dimension are unavailable rather than merely unchosen. The torch collector already ran: coverage.json shows all 60 CUDA kernels associated with zero unassociated or ambiguous kernels, so execution_timeline would only re-derive CPU-submit associations it already has, and it cannot bound GPU readiness or consumer completion anyway. The live uncertainty on the evaluated candidate is attribution, not scoring: measurement is valid and accepted (3.4018 ms vs paired parent 3.6847 ms, quality pass), but coverage for bundle trial-a9f72afa23-param-f2e37a0c reports the same call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa under three inconsistent routes (captured, cuda_graph_replay, eager_fused_stem_pool) across two candidate invocations, and the evaluation interpretation explicitly warns these are candidate-reported telemetry needing independent corroboration. nsys is available (request.json tools.nsys) and is the matching instrument for graph-tracing and attribution questions: it can natively show whether CUDA graph capture and replay actually execute on this exact candidate, whether the fused stem+pool path runs as eager kernel launches, and where inter-kernel gaps or overlap sit, none of which candidate route labels or a plain Torch trace prove. python_runtime is selected for the complementary host-dispatch question: a 3.40 ms forward over ~60 associated kernels run through the eager transformers stack leaves the dispatch-vs-compute split open, and cProfile self/inclusive times (read only as relative host costs, never as clean scores or GPU durations, since it perturbs execution) indicate whether extending capture/fusion is worthwhile. binding_cost is omitted because binding is direct with no functional replacements and the clean paired measurement already contains any wrapper cost; device_telemetry is omitted because device-wide utilization/PCIe readings cannot attribute anything inside the synchronized forward. Revision is set to the single listed candidate revision f12635aeab45ee38bb106d310a6ceff09f2faf366dde6d423cf56a72d015f7d1, the evaluated candidate whose route uncertainty motivates this collection.
